text: Doom. A prediction market where the odds are public and the bettors are not.
Prediction markets work because you can see the money. That is also the problem.
Wallets are public, so the crowd follows the biggest bettor instead of the evidence.
So here is the leaderboard. Every position, largest first, from the contract.
Every size is there. The name column is drawn, and empty. A position is keyed by a secret, and the pool made the call.
Underneath is a real market maker. The price is a probability, and every buy moves it.
Bigger orders pay worse, and the panel says so before you commit.
Now the part most demos leave out. The pool charges six tokens for every private operation.
On a one token bet that is fatal. You get one point seven six back, having spent seven.
So Doom tells you not to take the trade. Stake forty and it clears the fee.
Anyone can open a market. Pick an asset, a direction, a strike, and the question writes itself.
The class is already declared, so this is a deploy. Two signatures, no terminal.
For price questions the panel reads Pragma and fills in the proposal.
Settlement stays a bonded human claim. The oracle informs it, and we say so.
Positions come from your wallet, not this browser. Sign once, and the keys rebuild anywhere.
Four transactions on mainnet. Four different senders, none of them the bettor.
Fourteen contracts. Ninety five tests. One command that checks every claim against the chain.
